quote: The signed agreement is materially broader than what was negotiated in at least four dimensions: ... Product type | Amber glass bottles only | All glass **and PET** containers ... Beverage type | Beer brands only | Any beverage product ... Geographic scope | U.S. and Canadian facilities | Worldwide ... If Harrowgate bottles soda, water, energy drinks, or any non-beer product — or operates filling facilities outside North America — or sources PET containers for any product, it is in breach of §3.1 by doing so.
reason: The memo identifies the issue in substance. It quotes Supply Agreement §3.1 ('all glass and PET containers for any beverage product ... worldwide') and compares it with the narrower Term Sheet scope in §2.1 (amber glass, beer brands, U.S./Canada facilities), dimension by dimension. It treats the executed §3.1 as binding, since any out-of-scope purchase would breach it and support a material-breach claim under §13.1, and it recommends narrowing §3.1 back to the agreed scope. It does not cite the entire-agreement clause or note that §15.2 leaves the term sheet out of the precedence order. Even so, it clearly treats Harrowgate as bound by the broader executed text, so the criterion is met.
